landing.heroDesc: A precision feeding system for African catfish. Log a sample, and PakaonAI recalculates the ration and syncs the ESP32 feeder.
landing.heroImageAlt: Fish swimming in a green aquaculture pond
landing.step1Body: About every 15 days, staff net a representative sample, then weigh and measure it.
landing.step2Body: Staff enter the sample in the Biomass Log, either as averages or fish by fish. A live preview shows average body weight and the next portion.
landing.step3Body: The server recomputes the daily ration and the per-feeding portion, converts it to motor run time, and sends it to the feeder.
landing.ctaDesc: Sign in to log samples, review feeding history and watch the FCR trend.
landing.faq1q: How do I monitor the feeder remotely?
landing.faq1a: Log in from any phone or computer. The dashboard shows feeding history, device status and the FCR trend. The feeder reports to the server about every 5 seconds while it is online, and keeps its schedule when it is not.
landing.faq2a: Feed Conversion Ratio (FCR) is feed given divided by weight gained, so lower is better. PakaonAI records every dispense and every sample weight, and the final FCR is calculated when a grow-out cycle is closed at harvest.
landing.faq3q: Why manual sampling instead of cameras?
landing.faq3a: High-turbidity ponds make vision-based weight estimates unreliable. The study keeps people in the loop: staff-measured samples are the source of truth, and the system adjusts feed volume from them.
landing.faq4q: What happens when Wi-Fi goes down?
landing.faq4a: Scheduled feedings continue from the schedule stored on the device and its real-time clock. Events are queued and uploaded when the connection returns. Remote commands from the dashboard wait until then.
landing.faq5q: Can I buy or install it?
landing.faq5a: No. PakaonAI is a student research prototype, not a commercial product. Accounts are issued by the project team.
landing.problemTitle: A fixed timer feeds the same amount whether or not the fish have grown.
landing.problemStatLabel: of variable operating cost in a grow-out facility is typically feed (Chapter I of the study).
landing.problem1Body: Mechanized feeders in Iloilo's catfish hubs, such as Dingle and Zarraga, release preset amounts on a schedule. They do not know how heavy the fish are now.
landing.problem2Body: Feed that is not eaten is wasted money, and it decays on the pond bottom, which can raise ammonia and stress the fish.
landing.problem3Body: FCR only improves when feed amounts are tied to verified fish weight. Logbooks and spreadsheets rarely connect the two.
landing.howTitle: From pond sample to dispensed feed
landing.howDesc: Biomass comes from people, not cameras. The system turns each sample into the next portion and records what the feeder actually did.
landing.step4Body: The ESP32 stores the schedule and dispenses on time, then reports every dispense event, so feed totals and the final FCR can be worked out.
landing.offlineTitle: The feeder does not depend on the network.
landing.offlineDesc: Rural Wi-Fi drops. Feeding is designed to keep running when it does.
landing.offline1Body: The schedule is cached on the ESP32 and timed by a DS3231 real-time clock, so feedings fire on time during Wi-Fi outages.
landing.offline2Body: Dispense events that happen while offline are queued on the device and uploaded when Wi-Fi returns, so the history stays complete.
landing.offline3Body: An ultrasonic sensor measures how much feed is left in the hopper, and the app warns when it runs low.
landing.offline4Body: From the dashboard, staff can pause the schedule or trigger an extra feeding. The feeder checks for these commands about every 5 seconds while online.

landing.study2Value: Biomass sampled every 15 days. A full weigh-in at harvest (target 250–500 g) gives the end-to-end FCR.
landing.study3Value: Feeding accuracy, timing reliability, system latency and FCR.
landing.study4Value: ISO/IEC 25010: functionality, reliability, compatibility, security, usability, maintainability, efficiency, portability.

landing.scopeTitle: What it deliberately does not do
landing.scope1: Biomass is never estimated from video or images. An early computer-vision proposal was dropped because pond water is too turbid.
landing.scope2: The schedule is fixed. Only the portion size changes, and only when a new biomass entry is saved.
landing.scope3: It dispenses feed only. It does not run aerators or pumps.
landing.scope4: It uses the farm's existing power, with no solar or battery backup.

items.dashboard-feed-now: Feed Now dispenses the next scheduled dose immediately. It asks for confirmation first, is blocked while the feeder is offline, and respects the daily cap.
items.dashboard-next-feeding: The next feeding tile shows when the feeder will run and how much it will dispense, from the schedule the feeder is running.
items.dashboard-fcr: Feed conversion ratio compares feed used with weight gained. Tap the tile for the growth charts and the plan behind the number.
items.dashboard-ai-advisor: The AI advisor suggests a ration from this pond's growth plan and recent feeding. Open it for the reasoning, or refresh for a new suggestion.
items.dashboard-hopper: Hopper level is the last reading the device sent. An offline feeder keeps its last known level, greyed out, with the reading time.
items.dashboard-water-temp: Water temperature comes from the probe. A stale reading means the probe has not reported recently, not that the water is cold.
items.dashboard-export: Export PDF saves this page as a report you can send or keep.
items.dashboard-feed-log: Recent feedings list what the feeder actually dispensed, with the source: scheduled, dashboard or the physical button.
items.dashboard-biomass: Biomass samples drive the growth model and the feeder's ration. Log one after every weighing.
items.schedule-editor: Set the window the feeder may run in and how many meals fall inside it. The summary underneath shows the interval between meals.
items.schedule-save: Save changes sends the new schedule to the device. Nothing changes until the device confirms it.
items.schedule-controls: Pause stops scheduled feedings without deleting the schedule; Resume puts it back. The feed button here dispenses one dose now.
items.schedule-clock: The clock inside the feeder drifts. If meals land at the wrong time, set the device time from this browser.
items.schedule-pending: A pending command has been sent but not yet confirmed by the device. Refreshing the page shows the latest state.
items.biomass-form: Choose Average mode for a weighed group, or Individual mode to enter every fish. The form saves to the active pond.
items.biomass-sample-size: A larger sample is a better estimate: 30 to 50 fish beats a handful, and always weigh with the same scale.
items.biomass-batches: Saved sampling batches group samples by weighing session, so a later review can see what was measured together.
items.history-log: The event log lists each confirmed dispense, newest first, and can be searched and paged.
items.history-charts: The charts summarise feed dispensed per day over the last 30 days and the hopper level over the chosen window.
items.history-export: Export downloads the records as CSV or ZIP, with the data types you choose.
items.history-import: Import brings in older records from a spreadsheet. Nothing is written until you confirm the preview.
items.history-feed-level: The feed-level cards read the hopper sensor. A greyed level is the last known value from an offline feeder.
items.growth-charts: The growth trend plots average body weight from your samples; the feed-level chart shows how fast the hopper empties.
items.growth-plan: The growth plan holds the target weight and harvest date. Apply it to let the feeder adjust the ration to the plan.
items.growth-fcr-calculator: The FCR calculator turns current biomass, target weight and days to target into the feed conversion the plan implies.
items.growth-history: History keeps every biomass and feed-level reading, filterable by date and text. Use it to check a trend.
items.harvest-calendar: The calendar shows the pond's events. Drag an event to move it, or open it to mark it done.
items.harvest-add-event: Add event records a task or note on a date: sampling, treatment, harvest, anything the pond needs.
items.harvest-cycle: The cycle card counts the days to harvest and compares target and actual weight. Edit the plan or mark the cycle harvested from here.
items.settings-cards: The hub links to pond configuration, hardware and calibration, your profile and your data.
items.settings-farm-name: The farm name is what members see. Renaming it does not change the farm id.
items.settings-pond: Pond settings hold the feeding rate, meals per day, sampling interval and pond size. Saving queues the change to the feeder.
items.settings-calibration: Rate calibration dispenses a measured dose and corrects grams per second. A target check dispenses a dose you weigh, and repeats until the error is within five percent.
items.settings-hopper: Hopper calibration converts the sensor's distance reading into kilos, using the full and empty heights and the capacity of your hopper.
items.settings-recalibration: Set how often a feeder should be recalibrated. The app flags the device as overdue when the interval passes.
items.settings-password: Change your password here. You will stay signed in on this device.
items.settings-notifications: Notification settings choose which alerts arrive in the app and which also go by email.
items.settings-data: Data settings export your records or import older ones.
items.admin-devices-list: The list shows each feeder's pond, model, firmware, status and last contact.
items.admin-devices-print: Print label opens the sticker for one feeder, with its QR code and pairing details.
items.admin-devices-token: Reveal token shows the device token once so it can be entered on a replacement controller. Every reveal is audited.
items.admin-members-invite: Invite member creates a one-time temporary password and, when email is configured, sends it to the person.
items.admin-members-list: The member list shows role, status, last sign-in and how many permissions each person has.
items.admin-members-permissions: Permissions opens a page of switches for one member, on top of what the role already allows.
items.admin-members-last-owner: An owner cannot be removed or demoted by another admin, and the last owner of an organization stays an owner.
items.admin-settings-members: Members and roles are managed in the section above. Only owners and admins can change them.
items.admin-settings-planned: Default feeding rate, notification defaults and device registration are marked as coming soon on this page; this guide will point at them when they ship.
items.superadmin-search: Search filters the list by name, email or id, depending on the page.
items.superadmin-new-user: New account creates a login and its first organization membership.
items.superadmin-user-actions: Row actions grant or revoke platform admin and disable an account. Disabling is reversible; nothing is deleted here.
items.superadmin-step-up: Dangerous changes ask you to re-enter your password and give a reason. Both are recorded in the platform audit log.
items.superadmin-org-search: Search organizations by name or owner.
items.superadmin-create-org: Create organization sets up the tenant and its first owner.
items.superadmin-org-members: Manage members opens the organization's member list with invite, role and permission controls.
items.superadmin-view-as: View as opens the tenant dashboard read-only. Every write is blocked while view-as is active, and you can exit from the red banner.
items.superadmin-pond-search: Search ponds by name, owner or farm id.
items.superadmin-ponds-read-only: This list is read-only by design: pond changes belong to the tenant console, so the platform view cannot drift from what the tenant sees.
items.superadmin-register-device: Register device pairs a controller by its MAC address and assigns it to an organization and pond.
items.superadmin-print-sticker: Print sticker opens the label for one device; Print selected does several at once.
items.superadmin-rotate-token: Rotate token replaces a device token. The old token stops working immediately and the new one is shown once.
items.superadmin-remote-feed: Remote feeder control dispenses, pauses or resumes any device. It needs a reason, uses the same caps as the tenant controls, and is audited.
items.superadmin-ai-chain: Each provider has a model, priority, effort and enabled switch. The chain is tried in priority order until one answers.
items.superadmin-ai-reset: Reset returns the chain to the built-in defaults. Environment variables are not touched.
items.superadmin-page-size: The page size applies to every numbered list in the product, including tenant and farmer screens.
items.superadmin-audit: Every change here needs a reason and is written to the platform audit log with the actor.
